paragraphs: Chapter 1120
Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (10)
Ugly.
Even after obtaining the power of the Sun God, all he could do was endless self-destruction. Even the way he regenerated was nauseating to watch.

The Coalition's Genesis Knights didn't spare Joshua a single glance. No matter how desperately he endured the pain and performed his self-destruction, they felt no gratitude, of course, and didn't even acknowledge him.
But Kelliark couldn't completely ignore Joshua. He had to use about one-thousandth of his combat consciousness to continuously generate the Dark Origin magic to annihilate him.
[Die! Just die, you monster bastard!]
Orgal's sword pierced Kelliark's chest.
He was now so old that his back was bent and his eyes were milky white, but his sword still held depth, pride, and his own complete conviction.
In other words, he was still strong.
Engraved in his mind were the hundreds of brutal defeats he had suffered across all dimensions, but those memories were, on the contrary, making him shine even brighter.
[Hehehe, it's been a long time since you've been stabbed this deeply by my sword, hasn't it?]
Instead of pushing Orgal away, Kelliark first spread a semicircular shield. To prevent Malugia and the other Genesis Knights from rushing in further.
Then, he violently grabbed the blade that had dug into his chest.
"You're hastening your end. You don't have that much time left anyway."
Kelliark's magic was pouring into the blade. Soon, as Orgal forcibly pulled the sword out of his chest, Orgal screamed, spewing blood from every orifice in his face.
[Keoheok!]

The magic of Light and Dark Origin had infiltrated Orgal's body through the sword. Nevertheless, Orgal did not let go of the sword, but Kelliark snorted as if finding him pathetic. The penetrating wound in his chest had already healed perfectly.

Clank-! The blade broke. And a space explosion spread from Orgal's right arm, which had been holding the sword. A scene followed where dozens of sharp magic tendrils tore the right side of Orgal's upper body to shreds.
"Orgal!"
The Genesis Knights were tearing through the shield and entering.
[I'm fine, strike him!]
He wasn't fine. With almost half of his upper body mangled and blown away, he was on the verge of his consciousness cutting out and returning every second.
Even in that state, he had shouted for them to aim for Kelliark.
The wound on Kelliark's chest had fully regenerated, but the fighting spirit Orgal had shown was by no means meaningless.
'It's only a very little, but Kelliark's reaction has slowed down...!'
As if one side of an iron fortress's wall had crumbled, the frequency with which the consecutively extended swords of the Genesis Knights reached Kelliark's body increased noticeably.
Light-Speed Thrust. Chiron's Runcandel secret technique, this time, pierced Kelliark's knee. Kelliark's body tilted to the right, and for a moment, he lost his balance.
He barely managed to block Barisada, which was falling towards his neck, with his hand. But he couldn't block Vahn's sword falling on the opposite side.
'Damn it!'

Grrrrrrrrk-! The blade, shining with lightning, dug about halfway into Kelliark's neck before its advance stopped. It wasn't Vahn who had stopped; it was Kelliark who had momentarily increased the density of his body.
Even Vahn was shocked at that point. Since she was born and held a sword, this was the first time she had pushed a blade into an opponent's neck and failed to cut all the way through.
"What are you so surprised about, Battle God? Surely you didn't believe you could cut my neck with just this?"
Kelliark flung the two of them away. Malugia and Haylin couldn't link up with them and readjusted their distance.
"I suppose so. But it seems even you have your limits. Seeing your surprised face."

At those words, Kelliark touched the wound where Vahn's blade had entered. It was regenerating quickly as magic filled it, but an uncomfortable and unfamiliar sensation seemed to sweep through his entire body.
A moment later, Kelliark was able to realize what the reason was.
'...Am I... getting tired?'
The sensation of fatigue.

Reactions becoming dull, the body becoming heavy, breathing becoming difficult. That sensation, which he thought he would never feel again from a certain point on, was creeping over his entire body. A fatigue far rougher than the moment he had allowed Jin's blow in the Empire rushed over him.

"Puhahaha, good. Keep doing that, push me further, make me realize that I can die at any time without the Origin Stone, shout that I am not an absolute being! And I, in turn, will become that much stronger."

As he shouted with a madman's laughter, the ground began to shake. The earthquake instantly spread throughout the entire battlefield and advanced without end, with the momentum to shake the entire Black Sea.

Kelliark's massive magic spheres, heavily pressing down on the sky, were also vibrating. Some of them cracked on the surface, pouring the viscous magic within onto the ground, and that magic soon took the form of a rushing river.
If one were swept up in that river even once, no one could survive.
Even Chiron and Vahn, and Malugia and Haylin, were adjusting their positions to avoid the river's flow. Orgal couldn't escape on his own, so his comrades moved him instead.
[Ugh... Luna... I can still fight. My consciousness is just a little in and out, that's all...]
"...I know, Orgal."
It wasn't an empty platitude. The Genesis Knights still needed Orgal. It would be the same even if he were in a more wretched state than this.
The rivers of death intertwined and tangled like snakes in a jar, and each time, a tide that seemed to split the sky rose.

Chiron couldn't close the distance with Kelliark for a while as he was busy offsetting some of it with Heaven-Splitting Thrust. Every time a shell of a magic sphere burst, a new river branch was created, and fortunately, the only one suffering from being swept away in it so far was Joshua.
[Gwoooooh... Guuuuk...]
The area where the Genesis Knights could stand was rapidly shrinking.

Moving the battlefield was impossible. Not only was there no way Kelliark would follow as intended, but their allies would immediately begin to be massacred. To Kelliark, it was an incomprehensibly amusing sentiment.
"Do you want to protect the people? But you will have no choice but to protect Lokia Ganesto, not the people. This will be fun to watch."
As Kelliark continued to speak, everyone engaged in the life-or-death struggle felt the air of the battlefield rapidly heating up.
Also, as if noon had suddenly arrived, the scenery began to brighten, and before a few seconds had passed, the battlefield was turning so white it was blinding.
"What is that?"
"The, the sun...?"
Those defending the central front, and the Genesis Knights, all looked up at the sky. Because all the light and heat were falling from the sky.
There was a sun there.
So huge that it couldn't even be taken in at a single glance, the lower tip of a flame orb was emerging from between the realm of the annihilated phoenixes.

It could only be called a sun. Those who were not particularly strong were already going blind just by reflexively looking at it. Their eyeballs were burning up, and the skin on their faces was melting away.
Annihilation Flame Orb - Demon God.
It was one of Kelliark Zipfel's ultimate techniques. Although the attribute representing Solderet's power, dark heaven, was not included, Kelliark was a person who had seen the true end of magic.
His Annihilation Flame Orb did not require shadow energy. On the contrary, if he had relied on shadow energy, it was a realm he could never have reached.
[This crazy...! Kuaaaargh!]

Even Murakan was experiencing the pain of his scales rising and his wings melting. He was protecting the allies from the highest point in the sky, so he was that much closer to the Annihiliation Flame Orb.
Murakan, engulfed in flames and plummeting, barely held onto his consciousness and looked at the rapidly approaching ground.
If he fell, none of those standing there could survive. Coughing up mouthfuls of black blood, Murakan once again unleashed True Dark Advent.
Only the darkness of shadow energy could save his allies. Naturally, Murakan trusted Lafrarosa and first laid down the darkness for the troops.
But the next moment, Murakan realized that the primary target of the Annihilation Flame Orb was not people.
'Not the troops, it was aiming for Lafrarosa!?'
Hwarururuk...!
Flames were blooming on the entire surface of Lafrarosa's shield. The concentrated heat of the Annihilation Flame Orb had melted the entire front of the shield.

The Demon Army's troops couldn't break through the gap. The Annihilation Flame Orb was burning everything without discriminating between friend or foe. Its primary target was just Lafrarosa; the majority of the troops would likely not survive from the heat that was just spreading passively.

Before even ten seconds had passed, beyond the shield, even the front armor was seen to be melting little by little. It was because even though a new shield was being formed continuously, it couldn't block all the heat pushing inside.
The grand sealing was in danger. Talaris, who was already performing the grand sealing in front of the workshop, was gritting her teeth against the unfamiliar heat that was suddenly rushing in.

It wasn't just because of the sensation of being hot. The Annihilation Flame Orb naturally had a small amount of Light and Dark Origin magic mixed in. Every time that magic flowed into Lafrarosa, it was precisely targeting only Talaris.
The moment Talaris fell, the consciousnesses of Ameris and Lokia could be irreversibly distorted.

Although Murakan was blocking it as best he could with his whole body, in the end, Lafrarosa had to change its position. That meant they had to abandon all the troops defending the ground and retreat.
'Dammit, if I had known it was aiming for Lafrarosa from the beginning, I could have bought a little more time. What should I do? Do I have no choice but to abandon all of them, really...!'
The moment Murakan thought that.

Suddenly, a being on the ground was seen flying up, confronting the sun head-on. Focal, the Ego of Maintenance. She seemed to be trying to handle the Annihilation Flame Orb all by herself with her arms wide open.

"Focal, as expected of the weak ego that tries to maintain the world. Did you choose annihilation because it was painful to see the mortals die? How foolish. Your choice will only bring your world to ruin more quickly."
At those words, Focal replied in a deadpan voice.
[Who on earth said anything about being annihilated? Kelliark. I have merely come to welcome, my darkest child, and the part of that child that resembles me.]
